conviction_note: The company's own quarterly filings show a full year of book-to-bill near 0.83 (backlog $214.6m to $165.9m while revenue sat at ~$70m every quarter), and the 10-K caps FY27 backlog shipments at >=$149m against $282m of FY26 revenue; with ~$16m of fixed quarterly opex against a 28% gross margin the breakeven is ~$56m of revenue, so Q1 FY27 is the first quarter where the run-off actually bites EPS -- sized at roughly a third of the 13.1% median historical reaction because four consecutive prints have already been negative and the stock sits 6% off its 52-week low, so a meaningful part of this is in the price.

findings.finding: Kewaunee ran a book-to-bill of roughly 0.83 for all of FY26 -- consolidated backlog fell $214.6m -> $205.0m -> $192.9m -> $183.2m -> $165.9m across five straight quarters (an accelerating burn, -$17.3m in Q4 alone) while quarterly revenue was held flat at $71.1m / $70.1m / $69.4m / $71.4m -- and the FY26 10-K states 'not less than 90% of our order backlog at April 30, 2026 will be shipped during fiscal year 2027', i.e. >=$149m of shipments from backlog against $282m of FY26 revenue; with FY26 opex of $63.7m (~$15.9m/quarter, largely fixed) and a 28.5% gross margin, breakeven revenue is ~$56m per quarter, so Q1 FY27 revenue anywhere in the $55-63m range against the $71.1m year-ago comp puts EPS near zero versus $1.04.
findings.why_not_priced: If this arithmetic were priced there would be a published FY27 revenue estimate below $240m and a sell-side note on the operating-leverage cliff; instead stockanalysis.com shows 'Analyst Forecast: Not available', the sweep found a single estimate, there is no conference call and no option chain, and the stock trades ~2,000 shares a day (368 shares today). Most tellingly, the 2026-06-23 release that disclosed the single largest backlog drop of the cycle produced only a -3.63% reaction, versus -21.23% and -13.08% on prior, smaller backlog disappointments -- that is not a market that has run the conversion math. And the stock at $36.01 is 11.2x trailing $3.22, which is not a multiple that embeds an EPS collapse.
findings.independence: The backlog chain comes from four separate 8-K exhibits rather than one document: Q1 FY26 ($205.0m) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55529/000005552925000033/prfy26q1earningsrelease.htm , Q2 FY26 ($192.9m) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55529/000005552925000051/prfy26q2earningsrelease.htm , Q3 FY26 ($183.2m) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55529/000005552926000006/prfy26q3earningsrelease.htm , Q4 FY26 ($165.9m, LPG $118.8m / International $47.1m) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/55529/000005552926000017/prfy26q4earningsrelease.htm . Note that the >=90% shipment statement and the $165.9m level are the same underlying fact as the Q4 release, so the 10-K and the Q4 8-K should be collapsed to one source; the four-quarter revenue-flat-while-backlog-falls series is the genuinely additive part.

findings.finding: US hot-rolled coil, the primary input to Kewaunee's steel laboratory casework and fume hoods, rose from ~$1,070/short ton at the start of Kewaunee's fiscal Q1 FY27 (SMU average, week of 2026-05-01) to $1,180/st by 2026-08-12, a four-year high with Section 232 at 50% -- a ~10% sequential input-cost step inside a quarter whose revenue is delivered against fixed-price project backlog booked 6-18 months earlier.
findings.why_not_priced: Steel prices are public but nobody maps them onto a $103m lab-furniture microcap with no analyst model; if this link were being made there would be a gross-margin-driven estimate cut, and there is no estimate to cut. Kewaunee already flagged 'higher input costs and tariff-related cost pressure' in the FY26 Q4 release, which is the wire version -- what is not in the wire is that the sharpest leg of the HRC move landed precisely inside the May-July quarter being reported tonight. I have sized this small deliberately: Q4 FY26 (Feb-Apr 2026) ran on $1,000-1,050 HRC and still posted the year's best gross margin of 29.7%, which is direct counter-evidence that the pass-through is manageable.
findings.independence: The May 2026 level is a different SMU article: https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/05/01/gap-between-us-hr-prices-imports-little-changed/ (2026-05-01, SMU average $1,070/st). Both URL paths carry /2026/ so neither is a relabelled 2025 story.

findings.finding: On 2026-06-30 CEO Thomas D. Hull III settled 54,388 shares of vesting performance RSUs (which paid out at 150% of target) and elected cash settlement for 17,000 of them at $36.25 rather than taking the stock, with a further 16,243 withheld for tax -- i.e. the CEO converted roughly 60% of a large equity vest away from shares at a price essentially identical to today's $36.01.
findings.why_not_priced: A cash-settlement election inside a Form 4 footnote is not picked up by insider-transaction aggregators as a sale (no open-market transaction code), so it never reaches a screen; if it had been read as a signal, the 2,000-share-a-day tape would show distribution in July, and it does not. This is the weakest of my three and I have sized it accordingly -- cash settlement is often a dilution- or tax-management choice by the company rather than a view by the executive, and I could not distinguish the two from the filing.

findings.finding: Counter-evidence, filed deliberately because it cuts against my main finding: Avantor -- whose VWR arm is the closest public proxy for the US lab distribution channel Kewaunee sells through (two domestic dealers plus a national stocking distributor were 34% of FY26 sales) -- reported on 2026-07-29, after Kewaunee last spoke, that VWR organic growth swung from -4.8% in Q1 to +1.7% in Q2 and raised full-year guidance; Dodge's institutional planning index was also +7.8% year over year in August 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: KEQU is flat over 20 days (-0.52%) and 6% off its 52-week low, so nothing in its price reflects a channel inflection at its distributors; if it did, the stock would have re-rated off the lows in August. This matters because two of KEQU's last seven prints were +26.08% and +35.38%, both on backlog/story turns -- a Q1 booking recovery that stabilises the July 31 backlog above $165.9m is a live tail I cannot rule out and have no direct evidence against.
findings.independence: Dodge Momentum Index, published 2026-09-08: https://www.construction.com/dodge-momentum-index-flat-in-august/ -- institutional planning +4.9% month on month and +7.8% versus August 2025, with education specifically called out as a stronger pipeline. Different publisher, different dataset, same direction.

baseline_tension: There is no skew and no implied move to check against, and the 20-day run-up of -0.52% is neutral -- but the stock is already 38% below its 52-week high, 6% above its 52-week low and has fallen on four consecutive prints, so my negative finding partly agrees with a market that is already leaning bearish; what is not in that positioning is the specific book-to-bill-0.83 arithmetic and the ~$56m quarterly breakeven, which is why I am still negative but at well under half the 13.1% median historical reaction rather than at it.
